newsitem.title: USA: Florida may seek Medicaid damages only since 1982.
newsitem.headline: Florida may seek Medicaid damages only since 1982.

text.p: A judge on Monday ruled the state of Florida may only seek damages dating back to 1982 in its Medicaid case against the tobacco industry.

In his ruling, Circuit Court Judge Harold Cohen cited a statute that bars a plaintiff from seeking to recover damages that took place more than 12 years before filing suit. But he said Florida had the right to go ahead with its case, which seeks to recover public funds spent on treating sick smokers.

Florida's right to prove it is entitled to more than $1 billion in current damages -- and $16 billion in future damages -- is based on the state's 1994 Medicaid Third-Party Liability Act, which also served as a basis for the current lawsuit.
Cohen has set aside eight days for pre-trial hearings in the Florida case, known as State of Florida vs. American Tobacco Co et al., now scheduled for jury trial on August 4.
